title: Slidecast — A Tour
subtitle: What it does and how to drive it

slides.title: Title — Slidecast
slides.heading: Slidecast
slides.subheading: Decks that work when the Wi-Fi doesn't
slides.byline: Press → or tap Next on your phone
slides.notes:
Welcome. This deck is both the documentation and a demonstration — every feature it describes is being used to show it to you.

If you're reading this on the phone remote, you're already using half of what's here. Press N on the projecting machine to show these notes on screen too.

slides.title: What it is
slides.heading: A presentation server with a phone remote

bullets.sub: No binary file to corrupt, no proprietary format, diffs cleanly in git
Notes, next-slide preview, and a jump list in your hand
Images and activities embedded — it runs with no network at all

slides.notes:
Three ideas, in order of how much they matter.

The third is the one that earns its keep: a deck you can open from a USB stick in a building with no working Wi-Fi.

slides.title: Section — Running it
slides.heading: Running it
slides.notes: layout: "section" — a divider. Use these to give a long deck some shape; people navigate by them without realising.

slides.title: The two commands
slides.heading: Two commands

left.body:
pixi run start

Serves the deck to the projector and a remote to your phone. Prints both addresses and a QR code.

right.body:
pixi run build

Writes every deck to build/ as a standalone file. No server needed to open it.

slides.notes:
layout: "two-content" — two independent regions side by side.

Start is what you use in the room. Build is what you do the night before, so there's a file on the laptop that works even if nothing else does.

slides.title: The two addresses
slides.heading: Two addresses

bullets.sub: Open on the machine driving the screen, then press F for fullscreen
Scan the QR code the server prints on startup

slides.body: Whoever advances — phone or laptop — everyone follows. The server holds the position, not the browser.
slides.notes: Why the server owns the state: a device that reconnects mid-presentation lands on the right slide instead of slide 1. It also means you can open the deck on a second screen and it stays in step.

slides.title: The remote
slides.heading: The remote
bullets: Full speaker notes for the current slide
A live preview of the next one
Jump list, theme picker, deck picker
Swipe, or use a Bluetooth clicker
slides.notes:
layout: "media-right" — the workhorse. Text one side, media the other; media-left mirrors it.

The remote holds a screen wake lock, so your phone shouldn't sleep while you're presenting.

slides.title: Section — Writing slides
slides.heading: Writing slides
slides.notes: Now the part you'll actually spend time in.

slides.title: Anatomy of a slide
slides.heading: Anatomy of a slide
slides.caption:
Pick a layout, fill the fields it uses. Skip any you don't need — nothing is required.

Text fields accept HTML, so emphasis and quotation marks behave.
slides.notes:
layout: "content-caption" — a wide media region beside a narrower text column.

Fields: eyebrow, heading, subheading, body, bullets, quote, image, media, images, left, right, caption, notes, tag, cls.

The Layout Gallery deck shows all fourteen layouts. Switch to it from the remote.

slides.title: Notes go in the JSON
slides.heading: Write the notes first
slides.body: Every slide carries a notes field. It shows on your phone and, with N, on screen.
slides.quote: The slide is for the room. The notes are for you.
slides.notes:
This is the argument for the whole tool.

Slides get overloaded because they're doing two jobs: showing the room something, and reminding the speaker what to say. Split those and the slides get quieter and better.

Notes accept HTML too — bold the thing you'll forget.

slides.title: Discussion slides
slides.heading: A slide that changes the room

right.body: Dark background. A question. People look up.

slides.notes:
layout: "comparison" — like two-content, but each side gets a subheading.

Adding "cls": "ask" inverts a slide to the dark treatment. Use it for questions and discussion stops — the change in the room is doing the work, not the words.

The remote flags these so you can see a discussion stop coming.

slides.title: A discussion slide
slides.heading: What would you cut from your last deck?
slides.body: This slide is cls: "ask". Notice the room got quieter.
slides.notes:
This is that slide. Give it a moment before moving on — the pause is the feature.

Combine ask with center for a question that fills the screen.

slides.title: Section — Making it yours
slides.heading: Making it yours
slides.notes: The customisation section.

slides.title: Themes
slides.heading: Themes

left.body:
Every colour and typeface comes from a token. One value restyles the whole deck.

Two ship: Paper and Georgia Tech. Add your own as an entry in themes.json — no code.

slides.notes:
Try it now: press T, or tap a swatch on the remote. Watch this slide change under you.

The Georgia Tech theme follows GT's published accessibility guidance, not just its palette — Tech Gold is used for rules and bullets but never for text, since GT flags it as inaccessible on light backgrounds.

slides.title: Text size
slides.heading: Size it for the room you're in
slides.body: Dim projector? Deep room? Resize the whole deck from 70% to 160% — headings, body, quotes, and bullets together.

bullets.sub: Set it from the back of the room, where you can actually judge it

slides.notes:
Try it now. The size flashes on screen so you can confirm it from a distance.

It's saved between runs, so set it once while pointed at the projector and it's still right when you start.

slides.title: Images are embedded
slides.heading: Images travel inside the file
slides.notes:
layout: "grid" — two to four images, optional captions. Four lay out as a 2×2.

These three are inside this file as data URIs. Anything over 2560px is downscaled first, so a phone photo doesn't add megabytes.

There is no images folder to forget on a USB stick.

slides.title: Embedded activity
slides.heading: Activities embed too
slides.notes:
This is a real activity — a local HTML file inlined as the iframe's srcdoc. It works with no network because it isn't fetching anything.

Sandboxed to allow-scripts: it runs its own code but can't reach the deck.

Careful: while you're clicking inside an activity, arrow keys go to it, not the deck. Advance from your phone.

(It's also a quiz on the previous slides. Answers: everything works offline except the YouTube embed and the remote itself.)

slides.title: External embeds
slides.eyebrow: The one thing that needs the network
slides.heading: External embeds
slides.body: A YouTube URL can't be embedded into a file. If it can't load, this slide shows a QR code instead of a blank frame — press R to retry.
slides.notes:
layout: "media-full" — media fills the slide, text sits in a gradient panel.

Use the /embed/ URL form, not the watch link.

pixi run build lists every slide like this one, so you know your network dependencies before you're standing in front of a room.

Embeds mount only while their slide is showing — otherwise a video would keep playing, audibly, after you moved on.

slides.title: Section — When things go wrong
slides.heading: When things go wrong
slides.notes: The part nobody writes documentation for.

slides.title: Failure modes
slides.heading: If something breaks

bullets.sub: Open the built file from build/ — no server, no network, everything embedded
The slide shows a QR code. Press R to retry.
Usually a server left running from before a change. Restart it — the deck will tell you if that's the cause.
The remote holds a wake lock, but reconnecting picks up the current slide anyway

slides.notes:
The honest one is the third. API routes are registered when the server starts, but templates are read per request — so a stale server can serve new buttons that post to endpoints it doesn't have.

Rather than failing silently, the deck now falls back to acting locally and says restart the server to sync.

slides.title: Keys and decks
slides.heading: Worth memorising

left.body:
← → navigate
N notes
B blank the screen
+ − 0 text size
T theme
R reload an embed
F fullscreen

right.body:
Slidecast — A Tour
This one.

Layout Gallery
All fourteen layouts, one per slide.

Switch between them from the remote.

slides.notes:
B is underused. Blanking the screen during a discussion pulls attention back to the room better than any slide can.

Now switch to the Layout Gallery from your phone — it picks up where this leaves off.

slides.title: Closing
slides.heading: Now go write something worth presenting.
slides.body: Start by copying a slide from the Layout Gallery.
slides.notes:
Close here.
